name: Teclistamab (BCMA x CD3 bispecific antibody)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Teclistamab is a BCMA-directed T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody for triple-class-exposed relapsed/refractory myeloma. BCMA is near-universally expressed; use is not by a selective biomarker. Physician decides.

premedications.name: CRS premedication (step-up doses)
premedications.notes: Corticosteroid, antihistamine, and antipyretic before each step-up dose and the first full dose, per labeling, to reduce cytokine-release-syndrome severity.

supportiveCare: Step-up (priming) dosing with inpatient monitoring for cytokine-release syndrome and immune-effector-cell neurotoxicity (ICANS) during initiation.
Infection prophylaxis (antiviral, PJP, and consider antibacterial) and immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinemia.
Continuous weekly dosing to progression once the maintenance dose is reached.
monitoring: CRS and neurotoxicity (ICANS) monitoring during step-up and first full dose
myeloma response markers per follow-up schedule

doseModificationRules.text: Hold teclistamab for cytokine-release syndrome or neurotoxicity; manage per grade (supportive care, tocilizumab, corticosteroids) and resume after recovery per labeling. Physician directs.

drugs.name: Teclistamab
drugs.notes: Maintenance teclistamab 1.5 mg/kg subcutaneously once weekly (shown here on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 21-day cycle; dosing continues weekly to progression). Initiation uses step-up (priming) doses of 0.06 mg/kg then 0.3 mg/kg before the first full 1.5 mg/kg dose, each with CRS premedication and inpatient monitoring; the engine computes the steady-state weekly maintenance dose. Dosing is by actual body weight. Own wording from standard-of-care knowledge; physician decides.

provenance.locator: teclistamab BCMAxCD3 bispecific, weekly maintenance dosing after step-up
